newsitem.title: CHINA: China unveils big corporate convertible bond issue.
newsitem.headline: China unveils big corporate convertible bond issue.

text.p: China announced on Thursday it would allow the issue of four billion yuan ($481.9 million) worth of convertible corporate bonds, pushing a whole new batch of state firms towards eventual public listings, analysts said.

If the experiment is successful, the move could lead to a fundamental shift in the funding of China's state enterprises, many of then cash-starved due to high levels of debt and tight credit, the analysts said.

China's has previously allowed only a handful of listed firms to issue convertible bonds. The Shanghai Securities News said some of China's 500 biggest firms would be selected for the convertible bond experiment.
The newspaper said only non-listed firms are eligible for the time being.

No details of the issues or the companies involved were available. There was no indication of when the issues would begin or whether any of them would be foreign currency denominated and therefore open to foreign investors.
"This means China will go ahead with the public listing of large numbers of new companies once these firms have issued shares (converted from the bonds)," said a banker with a major Chinese bank.

"It will gradually lead to fundamental changes in the funding of state enterprises, which has so far come almost entirely from state bank loans, resulting in a huge bad loan problem for the state banks," he added.

The issue of convertible bonds, leading to public listings, would put many of China's inefficient state enterprises under the cold scrutiny of investors and auditors for the first time, forcing them to become more efficient, the analysts said.

"Once convertible bonds can be issued on a regular basis, they will have a decisive impact on poorly managed state firms," said one banker. "The bond issues will make the firms open to the market and they will have to improve."
The bonds, if converted, will become shares in the issuing state firms which will then be listed on one of China's two stock exchanges, the Shanghai newspaper said.
A new set of rules on convertible bonds was also published on Thursday. These state that the bonds would be traded on the exchange expected to be used for the eventual share listing.
Bonds issued by unlisted firms will be converted only after a share listing takes place, while those issued by listed firms can only be converted six months after the issue.

Under the new rules, companies must have a minimum of three consecutive years of profits to be eligible to issue convertible bonds, which will have a duration of no less than three years and no more than five years.
The size of each issue must be at least 100 million yuan ($12 million) and the bonds are not allowed to carry a coupon rate exceeding the interest rate on bank deposits of a similar duration.
The State Council (cabinet), has empowered the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the top securities watchdog, to be in charge of the new issue, the newspaper said.
Officials with the CSRC declined to comment.
"There could be some foreign currency bonds issued by some joint-venture companies such as Shanghai Volkswagen Co," one industry analyst said.
